title: A new quantitative theorem for smooth exponent geometry
objective: Prove a genuinely new quantitative theorem about the exponent-lattice structure underlying fixed-prime smooth-number prefixes, resolving or strictly improving a published counting or algorithmic bound. Produce a complete proof, a precise comparison with the strongest relevant literature, reproducible supporting evidence and an honest paper explaining the mathematical advance.
acceptance_criteria: State a uniform theorem for an infinite family with an explicit quantitative improvement over the strongest verified published result, or settle a recognized open structural question with a substantive counting or algorithmic consequence.
Give a complete proof; numerical agreement, isolated examples and routine consequences of known theorems do not satisfy the goal.
Document the closest prior definitions and theorems, their hypotheses and exactly where the new argument improves them. An unsuccessful search is not evidence of novelty.
Explain the contribution to an existing mathematical problem without claiming a prime-distribution consequence that has not been proved.
Prepare a reproducible, internally checked manuscript only after the mathematical and priority checks succeed. Submission readiness and publication are not guaranteed.

first_candidate.problem: Determine the asymptotic number of three-dimensional corner cuts of a given cardinality.
first_candidate.definition: For d >= 2 and n >= 1, C_d(n) counts distinct sets D = {a in Z_{>=0}^d : w dot a < t} of cardinality n, where each w_i > 0 and the separating hyperplane contains no nonnegative lattice point. Count sets, not their internal orderings or their prime realizations.
first_candidate.connection_to_project: An exponent prefix over distinct primes is a corner cut with weights log(p_i). Conversely every finite corner cut can be realized over distinct ordered prime bases above any prescribed lower bound. Thus the corner-cut count is exactly the number of available smooth-prefix shapes as bases vary, not the number of orders, realizing tuples or prefixes of one fixed tuple. This is neither an unranking speedup nor a new prime-distribution estimate.

verified_published_baseline.author: Uli Wagner
verified_published_baseline.general_bounds: For fixed d >= 2: Omega_d(n^(d-1) log n) <= C_d(n) <= O_d((n log n)^(d-1)).
verified_published_baseline.dimension_two: C_2(n) = Theta(n log n), attributed in Wagner's abstract to Corteel et al. (1999).
verified_published_baseline.dimension_three: Omega(n^2 log n) <= C_3(n) <= O(n^2 (log n)^2).
verified_published_baseline.verification_scope: The primary published abstract was inspected directly, and the lower and upper proofs were reconstructed from the author's full thesis Chapter 3. The later primary comparisons and their precise reading scopes are recorded in results/research/corner_cut_growth_audit.json. These are verified source comparisons, not an unrestricted claim about all current work.

first_candidate.success_target: If the gap survives the literature audit, close it or strictly narrow it by a uniform asymptotic bound. A concrete sufficient improvement would be C_3(n) = Omega(n^2 (log n)^(1+delta)) or C_3(n) = O(n^2 (log n)^(2-delta)) for an explicit fixed delta > 0. The ideal outcome is a matching order of growth with a proof mechanism that extends beyond isolated examples.
first_candidate.current_open_status: The inspected same-object published lower/upper gap is closed by the complete main proof. The final internal novelty and usefulness assessment supports presenting the matching lower count as a new result under the documented source comparison.

proposed_proof_route.definition: For a two-dimensional corner cut T with 1 <= |T| <= n, let F_n(T) count three-dimensional n-point corner cuts B with B intersect {z=0} = T.
proposed_proof_route.known_route: The lifting argument gives at least one completion of each T and hence the lower bound obtained by summing C_2(j) for j <= n.
proposed_proof_route.attribution: Restriction, lifting and the possibility of gaining a logarithmic factor from average completion multiplicity are already discussed in Wagner's thesis. The fiber viewpoint alone is not a new contribution.
proposed_proof_route.next_mathematical_test: Reconstruct that argument and seek a duplicate-controlled construction with logarithmically many completions on average, or identify a new obstruction supporting a sharper upper bound. A claimed family must include an injectivity or multiplicity proof.
proposed_proof_route.caution: Do not conjecture logarithmically many completions for every T: if |T| = n then its only completion is T in the z=0 plane.
proposed_proof_route.thesis_access_status: The complete Chapter 3 lower-bound, upper-bound and remarks arguments were read through a full-text mirror, with allowance for OCR errors. Direct institutional PDF retrieval still timed out.

prime_base_realization.statement: Every nonempty finite corner cut is realizable as a smooth-number exponent prefix over distinct ordered prime bases, all above any prescribed bound B.
prime_base_realization.proof_location: paper/corner_cut_growth/main.tex, Section sec:primeheight, Lemma lem:linear-score and Theorem thm:height; qualitative realization attributed to Vietri Proposition 6.2.
prime_base_realization.arithmetic_input: Classical Bertrand postulate; for sorted positive weights choose disjoint intervals (2^(i-1) exp(T w_i), 2^i exp(T w_i)).
prime_base_realization.source_inspected: Published text pp. 197--198, stating and completing the proof of Bertrand's postulate.
prime_base_realization.consequence: For every fixed B, S_{d,B}(n)=C_d(n), where S counts distinct prefix exponent sets over varying ordered tuples of distinct primes greater than B. Hence the cumulative theorem counts exactly the realizable smooth-prefix shapes.
prime_base_realization.scope: Consequence of Vietri (2002), Proposition 6.2, including the arbitrary lower prime bound via its proof. Varying prime tuples are essential. No separate novelty, prime-distribution or unranking claim.

prior_art.specialization: Impose comparisons between included points and the finite minimal excluded border; for a prescribed internal order add consecutive comparisons. Enlarge the original scaling to exceed any B.

fixed_cardinality_literature_comparison.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Fixed-cardinality comparison and the average-completion consequence
fixed_cardinality_literature_comparison.exact_reduction: C_d(n) equals the number of n-sets of {0,...,n}^d containing the origin. Positivity and exclusion of the infinite complement follow from the n+1 axis points. This is a standard finite-ground-set reduction, not a novelty claim.
fixed_cardinality_literature_comparison.total_count_boundary: The rectangular-grid threshold count of Haukkanen--Merikoski sums every included cardinality. In dimension two its value on {0,...,n}^2 is Theta(n^4), whereas C_2(n)=Theta(n log n). Its total-count lower estimate does not supply a lower estimate for this selected origin class.
fixed_cardinality_literature_comparison.recognition_boundary: Coeurjolly et al. use two leaning polygons to describe feasible plane parameters. Boundary-point recognition is established background; the claimed advance is the prescribed-size bounded-normal injection and its multiscale counting consequence.

average_completion_consequence.statement: For every fixed d>=2, the mean number of n-point d-dimensional completions over all nonempty (d-1)-dimensional corner cuts of size at most n is Theta_d(log n).
average_completion_consequence.proof: The restriction fibres partition all n-point cuts. Divide the matching count in dimension d by its summed counterpart in dimension d-1; for d=2 use A_1(n)=n.
average_completion_consequence.source_location: Section 3.5, Weakness of the lower bound
average_completion_consequence.attribution: Restriction, lifting, the fibre identity and the suggestion of logarithmic mean multiplicity are Wagner's. The corollary is a consequence of the matching count, not an independent novelty claim.
average_completion_consequence.limit: This is not a bound for every individual slice: a slice of size n has exactly one n-point completion.

prime_height_candidate.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Candidate 25: sharp worst-case prime size for finite-prefix realization
prime_height_candidate.definition: H_d(n,B) is the worst, over ordered length-n prefixes of global monomial orders, of the least log(max p_i) among realizing distinct prime tuples above B.
prime_height_candidate.statement: For fixed d>=2, H_d(n,B)=Theta_d(n log(max(B,2))), uniformly for n>=2 and B>0. The same worst-case order holds for underlying corner-cut sets.
prime_height_candidate.explicit_upper: Put c_d=d(d!)^2 2^(d-1), a=max(30,d,log(max(B,2))+1). Then log(max p_i)<(a+log 2)(c_d n+1)+1.
prime_height_candidate.explicit_lower: The axis prefix 0,e_1,...,(n-1)e_1 forces log(max p_i)>=(n-1)log(max(B,2)).
prime_height_candidate.key_structural_step: A strict integer-score prefix with cutoff S satisfies lcm(A_i,A_j)>S. After sorting weights, all but the smallest satisfy A_j^2>n-1.
prime_height_candidate.mechanism: Use the existing linear integer-score certificate; anchor the smallest weight at a Bertrand prime exactly; realize all other coordinates in disjoint Dusart short intervals with positive errors whose total on an included exponent vector is less than one scaled score gap.

vasiliev_pavlov_2009_full_text_review.parameter: Degree n is the number of monomials in the chain, not polynomial total degree; variables remain labeled.
vasiliev_pavlov_2009_full_text_review.exact_common_class: Definition 5, p. 80: strictly admissible finite orderings are initial intervals of global admissible monomial orders. This is exactly the positive-weight ordered-prefix family O_d(n), using the known finite Robbiano representation.
vasiliev_pavlov_2009_full_text_review.class_distinction: Definition 4 finite local admissibility is broader. Remark 1 gives 1<x<x^2<y<y^2, which cannot be an initial interval because xy is missing. Relevant strict-prefix counts are Tables 7--8, not Tables 5--6.
vasiliev_pavlov_2009_full_text_review.known_methods: Sections 3--6 establish recursive border/front enumeration, finite weight cones and reduced feasibility comparisons. These objects, methods and scalar representation are prior art.
vasiliev_pavlov_2009_full_text_review.counting_comparison: Section 7 and Tables 7--8 report finite values, but no uniform asymptotic strict-prefix or corner-cut count. No theorem or argument giving the multiscale prescribed-size lower bound was found in the full paper.
vasiliev_pavlov_2009_full_text_review.arithmetic_comparison: Section 10 uses normalized integer normals and exact arithmetic, but states no uniform integer-certificate-size or realizing-prime-height theorem. The paper contains no prime-realization theorem.
vasiliev_pavlov_2009_full_text_review.algorithmic_comparison: Recursive enumeration and implementation are presented without a uniform cardinality-asymptotic, delay/runtime, weight-height or prime-height bound implying our proposed quantitative conclusions.
